title: 802.1X and MAB on a switch port
domain: Secure Network Access, Visibility, and Enforcement
blurb: Make an access port authenticate users with 802.1X and fall back to MAB for devices that can't.
purpose: A switch port with no access control lets anyone who plugs in onto the network. This lab sets up 802.1X for managed laptops, with MAB as the fallback for printers and phones that can't run 802.1X, so ISE decides who gets access. It covers network access control on the switch side.
scenario: Port **GigabitEthernet1/0/10** on access switch SW1 feeds a desk shared by employee laptops and a network printer. The laptops have an 802.1X supplicant. The printer has none. Configure the switch so that ISE at **10.10.99.10** (RADIUS key **R4diusKey**) authenticates whatever connects, and data VLAN **10** is used once access is granted.
objectives: Name the three 802.1X roles and put the exchange in order
Point the switch at ISE with RADIUS
Configure the port for 802.1X first, then MAB

steps.title: Know the roles
steps.learn: 802.1X has three roles. The **supplicant** is software on the endpoint. The **authenticator** is the switch or wireless controller, which relays EAP and opens the port. The **authentication server** checks the credentials and returns the result.
steps.task: Match each device in the topology to its 802.1X role.

steps.title: Put the 802.1X exchange in order
steps.learn: Between the endpoint and the switch, EAP travels as **EAPOL** frames. Between the switch and ISE, it travels inside **RADIUS** packets. The switch never sees the password, it only relays.
steps.task: Arrange the steps of an 802.1X login from first to last.
steps.question: Order the exchange, from link up to access granted.
steps.hint: The switch asks who you are, relays your answer to ISE, and the protected EAP method runs before ISE decides.
items: The link comes up, and the switch sends EAP-Request/Identity
The switch wraps the response in a RADIUS Access-Request to ISE
ISE and the laptop negotiate an EAP method and run it (for example PEAP or EAP-TLS)
ISE sends RADIUS Access-Accept with the authorization result
The switch authorizes the port and sends EAP-Success

steps.title: Point the switch at ISE
steps.learn: 802.1X needs RADIUS. Define the server with its ports and key, group it, and create the method lists. `aaa authorization network` lets ISE push the VLAN, ACL or SGT, and accounting tells ISE when sessions start and stop.
steps.task: Turn on AAA. Define RADIUS server **ISE** at **10.10.99.10** on auth port **1812** and acct port **1813** with key **R4diusKey**, put it in group **ISE-RADIUS**, and create the **default** dot1x authentication, network authorization and dot1x start-stop accounting lists for that group.
steps.hint: `aaa new-model`, `radius server ISE` with `address ipv4 10.10.99.10 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813` and `key R4diusKey`, then `aaa group server radius ISE-RADIUS` with `server name ISE`, then `aaa authentication dot1x default group ISE-RADIUS`, `aaa authorization network default group ISE-RADIUS` and `aaa accounting dot1x default start-stop group ISE-RADIUS`.

commands.explain: Turns on the AAA framework.
Defines a RADIUS server named ISE.
Sets the server address and the standard RADIUS ports for authentication (1812) and accounting (1813).
Sets the shared secret that must match ISE.
Creates a RADIUS server group named ISE-RADIUS.
Adds the ISE server to the group.

commands.cmd: aaa authentication dot1x default group ISE-RADIUS
commands.explain: Sends 802.1X authentication requests to ISE.

commands.cmd: aaa authorization network default group ISE-RADIUS
commands.explain: Lets ISE return authorization settings such as VLANs and ACLs.

commands.cmd: aaa accounting dot1x default start-stop group ISE-RADIUS
commands.note: The switch can now use ISE for 802.1X and MAB.
commands.explain: Sends session start and stop records to ISE.

steps.title: Turn on 802.1X globally
steps.learn: Port settings have no effect until 802.1X is switched on for the whole switch.

commands.explain: Turns 802.1X on for the whole switch. Without it, the port settings do nothing.

steps.title: Configure the access port
steps.learn: With `authentication port-control auto`, the port starts **unauthorized** and passes only EAPOL until a session is approved. `mab` uses the endpoint's MAC address as its identity when no supplicant answers. `authentication order dot1x mab` tries 802.1X first, and `authentication priority dot1x mab` lets a laptop that starts 802.1X later take over from a MAB session.
steps.task: On **GigabitEthernet1/0/10**: make it an access port in **VLAN 10** with PortFast, set it as an 802.1X **authenticator** with port control **auto**, turn on **MAB**, and set both the **order** and the **priority** to dot1x, then mab.
steps.hint: `interface GigabitEthernet1/0/10`, `switchport mode access`, `switchport access vlan 10`, `spanning-tree portfast`, `dot1x pae authenticator`, `authentication port-control auto`, `mab`, `authentication order dot1x mab`, `authentication priority dot1x mab`.

commands.explain: Enters configuration for the port where the user connects.
Makes the port an access port, which 802.1X requires.
Puts the port in VLAN 10 by default.

commands.note: PortFast skips listening and learning, so the endpoint isn't held for 30 seconds before it can authenticate.
commands.explain: Brings the port up immediately instead of waiting for spanning tree, so authentication doesn't time out.
Makes the switch the 802.1X authenticator on this port.

commands.note: The port waits for a successful authentication before passing traffic.
commands.explain: Turns on authentication. The port stays closed until the device is authenticated.
Turns on MAC Authentication Bypass for devices that can't do 802.1X.
Tries 802.1X first, then MAB.
Lets 802.1X take over if a device that passed MAB later starts 802.1X.

steps.title: What happens to the printer?
steps.question: The printer is plugged into Gi1/0/10. It never answers the EAP-Request/Identity. What happens?

options.text: After the 802.1X timeout, the switch tries MAB and sends the printer's MAC address to ISE as its identity.
The port stays unauthorized for good, because dot1x is first in the order.
options.why: With `mab` and `authentication order dot1x mab`, the switch falls back to MAB once 802.1X times out.

options.text: The switch opens the port in VLAN 10 with no check.
options.why: Port control auto never opens the port without a successful authentication, unless you configure open mode.

options.text: ISE sends the printer an EAP-Request.
options.why: ISE never talks to the endpoint directly. The switch is the authenticator.

steps.title: Check the session
steps.task: Show the authentication session details for **Gi1/0/10**.
steps.hint: `do show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet1/0/10 details`. Short forms like `do sh auth sess int g1/0/10 det` work too.

commands.cmd: show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet1/0/10 details

commands.note: jdoe authenticated with dot1x, so MAB was never needed, and the port is authorized in VLAN 10.
commands.explain: Shows the session on the port: which method succeeded and what ISE returned.

summary: RADIUS to ISE with dot1x authentication, network authorization and accounting lists, 802.1X turned on globally, and an access port that authenticates with 802.1X first and falls back to MAB.
